Understanding the estimate

Enter patient data to see the main influences on this prediction.
Longer bar = larger increase in predicted risk

Up to 5 factors increasing predicted mortality, ranked by their exact TreeSHAP contribution (log-odds, averaged across the 10 imputation models), shown as the change in calibrated risk when that contribution is removed. pp = percentage points.

SHAP values are relative to the average prediction of the training cohort. Converted pp effects do not add up exactly (non-linear scale) and do not imply causation.

0%5%10%15%
Less importantMore important

Each variable’s share of total XGBoost Gain (summed across the 10 imputation models). All 32 variables sum to 100%. These percentages describe model importance, not mortality risk.

Gain is a global XGBoost importance measure. It can be influenced by correlation and the number of available split points; it is not a causal ranking.

View all risk bands
Risk-based clinical guidance
Risk groupSuggested clinical action
Low <5%Continue standard treatment and monitoring; the model helps flag low-risk patients so that unnecessary escalation can be avoided.
Moderate 5–<15%Monitor more closely, reassess risk as new data emerge, and optimize modifiable factors.
High 15–<30%Consider increased surveillance and early specialist consultation; assess the need for intensive care or early intervention.
Very high ≥30%Priority assessment with continuous monitoring; consider ICU / step-up care and a prognostic discussion appropriate to the clinical context.

Risk bands are illustrative research thresholds and require external validation. Predicted mortality alone does not determine ICU admission.
